science_relevance.scientific_problem: Construct large subsets of F₃ⁿ without nontrivial three-term arithmetic progressions.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Explicit cap sets establish lower bounds in additive combinatorics and clarify the possible density of progression-free sets. The local eight-dimensional construction contributes a finite instance of this mathematical question.

papers.title: New Lower Bounds for Cap Sets
papers.task_relation: Tyrrell constructs larger cap sets to improve mathematical lower bounds. This task searches F₃⁸ using a greedy priority rule; the finite dimension and search mechanism are local restrictions of the same cap-set construction objective.
papers.primary_goal: Improve lower bounds on the largest cap sets through new constructions.

science_relevance.reason: Primary research addresses the underlying problem directly; scientific importance does not rely on the agent/framework paper.
science_relevance.definition: A task is important to science when it addresses a substantive scientific or real-world problem, and a cited research paper's main objective is to solve that problem or advance understanding of it. The evidence must explain why the problem matters and how the local task represents it. Using a task to evaluate an agent, framework, or general-purpose model, or citing only a benchmark, dataset, or tool, does not establish scientific importance.
